column1: # O1: Update, Setup, Learn rows (groups of the restructured hub; see the header of ../hub and groups.tsv)

column9: One install run, started by you: free-space check, Arch news, pacman cache prune, keyring first, pacman + AUR (no PKGBUILD review), flatpak, rustup/cargo, npm -g (Codex, Gemini), pipx/uv, Go tools, Claude Code, nvim (lazy lock commit, Mason, treesitter), oh-my-zsh, tpm; then pacnew, reboot hint, failed units. No sleep while it runs; log in ~/.local/state/sysup/last.log. The packages are downloaded in the background beforehand.
Looks for pending repo, AUR, flatpak and npm updates and refreshes the waybar badge; installs nothing. A user timer does the same every two hours.
The typescript of the last sysup install run (less; paste it into an agent when a run failed).

column6: +pause bash -c 'systemctl list-timers dotfiles-predownload.timer --no-pager; echo; cat /var/lib/dotfiles-predownload/state 2>/dev/null | sed -n "1s/.*/last run (epoch): &/;2s/.*/packages: &/;3s/.*/result: &/"; echo; sysup status'
column9: The root timer dotfiles-predownload downloads pending pacman updates into /var/cache/pacman/pkg (and flatpak commits) without installing. Enabled by sudo ./apply-system.sh --only services.
Lists firmware updates from LVFS for this machine. Changes nothing; firmware is never part of sysup.
Interactive. BIOS/EC updates need AC power and a battery above 30 %, and usually a reboot.

column3: Downgrade a package (from the pacman cache)
column9: Rollback: pick an installed package, then a cached older version (AUR tool downgrade; the cache keeps the previous two versions). The Update group also offers to install the tool when it is missing.
Config files that a package update left as .pacnew; sysup lists them at the end of a run.
One-time: asks the server URL and e-mail (kept in ~/.config/rbw, never in the repo), logs rbw and bw in.
Recreates ~/.local/state/theme/current (black) when it is missing or broken.

column3: Apply browser settings (Zen user.js, Chrome flags)
column9: Copies the tracked Zen and Chrome settings into the flatpak sandboxes (merge, idempotent).
Symlinks new files of the repo into $HOME.
The architecture notes of this dotfiles repo: layout, theme, bar, hub, greeter, users.
